questions.title: Who will receive the longest prison sentence at the trial over the July 2023 burglary of Gianluigi Donnarumma's Paris home?
questions.background: Goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and his partner were attacked during a burglary at their Paris home in July 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Paris Criminal Court's judgment, as documented by the court or reliable contemporaneous reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the defendant receiving the longest total prison sentence in the trial verdict delivered by September 30, 2026. Compare sentences actually imposed, including any suspended portions, rather than sentences requested by prosecutors. Later appeals do not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The defendant's name as publicly reported.
questions.current_reasoning: July 11, 2026 AFP/Le Parisien/L'Equipe reporting officially confirmed the Paris Criminal Court (tribunal correctionnel) trial of the three adult defendants for September 10-11, 2026, eliminating postponement risk past Sept 30. The two minor suspects were already tried separately in juvenile court in early July (receiving 4 and 3 years, including 1 year suspended), so they are definitively excluded. The July 11 indictment details further strengthen Ilyas Kherbouch's ('Ganito', 21) position as clear favorite for the longest sentence: beyond his principal-mastermind designation, 7-year prior for the Simone Zanoni home-jacking, and March 2026 Villepinte prison escape, investigators attributed direct SMS instructions on the eve and night of the burglary to his line and found photos of the bloodied, sequestered third adult defendant on Kherbouch's phone. Co-mastermind Khyan M. ('Kiki', 21) remains reported solely with an initialed surname (0.10, with 0.12 left for Khyan M.'s full surname if published at trial, a tie, or the third defendant).

local_articles.title: Gaza Cinema Academy launches at Venice Film Festival with celebrity backing
local_articles.snippet: DUBAI: The Gaza Cinema Academy has been officially launched at the Venice Film Festival with the aim of creating a lasting platform for film education, training and production for Palestinians in Gaza. Film industry insiders from Ramy Youssef to Kaouther Ben Hania, whose films have earned Oscar nods, have lent their backing to the project. The initiative was unveiled on Monday by Palestinian filmmakers Ezzaldeen Shalh and Mai Masri, who co-founded the academy as a space designed to help emerging filmmakers develop their skills and tell stories from their own perspectives. Film heavyweights Annemarie Jacir, Hiam Abbass and Saleh Bakri have also got behind the initiative. questions.title: Who will win Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election?
questions.background: Okinawa is Japan's southernmost prefecture, where the presence of US military bases is a major political issue.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official results announced by Okinawa's election authorities, either directly or as reported by reliable news organizations. Resolution : The question resolves when the winner of Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election is officially announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major final-weekend polling sweep published Sept 6 (one week before Sept 13 voting) shifts the race decisively toward five-party-backed challenger Genta Koja (0.53 -> 0.63) over two-term All-Okinawa incumbent Denny Tamaki (0.46 -> 0.365; 0.005 across four minor candidates): (1) Yomiuri Shimbun (Sep 3-6, phone+net, n=1,410) reports Koja clearly leading ('先行') with Tamaki trailing—noting 20% of 2022 Tamaki voters switched to Koja, 80% of 2022 Shimoji voters back Koja, and economy/prices (75%) dwarfs bases (45%); (2) Asahi Shimbun / Okinawa Times / QAB (Sep 5-6, phone+net) similarly reports Koja slightly ahead ('やや先行') with Tamaki chasing vigorously (40% undecided)—a striking signal given Okinawa Times/Asahi's historically All-Okinawa-favorable coverage; (3) Kyodo / Ryukyu Shimpo / OTV (Sep 5-6, pure RDD phone, 603 landline + 404 mobile) shows a dead heat ('横一線', <10% undecided), yet its internals also favor Koja: economy/tourism/jobs is the #1 issue (46%, breaking 70% Koja) vs bases (26%, breaking 80% Tamaki), and Henoko relocation support edges opposition 48%-46%. We cap Koja at 0.63 (leaving Tamaki 0.365) because pure phone polls remain tied, Tamaki leads ~60% of independents and 70+ voters (who turn out at higher rates), and 20-40% remain undecided in Yomiuri/Asahi.
